crossrefs.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’
Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’
He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
And now, O Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God by walking in all His ways, to love Him, to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.
“Right, Teacher,” the scribe replied. “You have stated correctly that God is One and there is no other but Him,
The LORD your God will circumcise your hearts and the hearts of your descendants, and you will love Him with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.
But if from there you will seek the LORD your God, you will find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
But Jesus answered, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
do not harden your hearts as you did at Meribah, in the day at Massah in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested and tried Me, though they had seen My work.
So I gave you a land on which you did not toil and cities that you did not build, and now you live in them and eat from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.’
do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.

notes.title: Tested in the wilderness, answering from Deuteronomy

crossrefs.text: I will give them one heart and one way, so that they will always fear Me for their own good and for the good of their children after them.
The LORD will protect and preserve him; He will bless him in the land and refuse to give him over to the will of his foes.
In the future, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you are to tell him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD your God swore to give your fathers,
be sure to return it to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you, and this will be credited to you as righteousness before the LORD your God.
And now, O Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you but to fear the LORD your God by walking in all His ways, to love Him, to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
and to keep the commandments and statutes of the LORD that I am giving you this day for your own good?
Because they were ignorant of Godʼs righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to Godʼs righteousness.
